rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A 10-minute gradient provides a useful resolution baseline near the scoring time target.
Change only gradient duration to identify which critical pairs respond to a shallower slope. The modest extension should keep the last peak close to 10 minutes while improving separation.

The nearly coeluting late pair did not improve with a shallower gradient, so test temperature-driven selectivity while holding the gradient fixed. Higher temperature should also create time headroom for further resolution optimization.

Test the opposite temperature limit because heating worsened selectivity in the early cluster without resolving the late coelution. Keeping the gradient unchanged isolates temperature effects and should leave the last peak near 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction to remove low-organic time while making the gradient shallower at the favorable low temperature. This tests whether a shifted gradient window can improve the late critical pairs without pushing the last peak beyond 10 minutes.

Shift the window upward again and reduce its slope to spread the remaining critical pairs while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes. The first peak at 1.28 minutes provides some room to increase starting organic, but early-pair compression will be monitored.

Test a narrower, shallower gradient to improve the late cluster and reveal whether shifting the starting composition changes its near-coelution. This is an exploratory step because the early cluster may compress or reorder.

Return to the best starting composition and make the gradient slightly shallower by lowering its endpoint. This should improve the middle and late critical pairs while using the roughly half-minute headroom before the time penalty begins.

Test an intermediate starting composition with a shallower slope, aiming to improve the late cluster while keeping the final peak near 10 minutes. This will locate the tradeoff between late-pair gains and the early-pair compression seen at phi0 0.40.

Test a slightly lower starting composition to strengthen the middle critical pair and avoid early-cluster compression. The slope is chosen to keep the last peak near 10 minutes while retaining most of the late-pair separation.

Test a modest temperature increase within the optimized window rather than the original broad gradient. This will show whether temperature can improve the remaining middle-pair selectivity while creating time headroom without sacrificing the resolved early cluster.

Test whether a terminal hold changes selectivity in the stubborn late cluster, which has barely responded to temperature or gradient slope. The stronger initial slope should limit total retention, though the lower endpoint may introduce a time penalty.

Explore beyond the compressed early-cluster region to check whether elution-order changes reopen those separations. The much shallower gradient also tests whether the stubborn late pair can gain meaningful resolution in a different solvent window.

Refine near the best gradient slope using a shorter programmed gradient and a terminal hold. The slope should keep the critical cluster close to its best separation, while the 0.65 endpoint tests whether the last peak remains below 10 minutes.

Test a lower starting composition with a slope between the earlier broad-window methods and the current optimum. This may bring the middle critical pair above 1.5; the endpoint is high enough to limit, though not eliminate, the terminal-hold time cost.

Combine a slightly shallower slope with a small temperature increase to target improved critical-pair separation while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes. This probes the local balance between resolution gains and the onset of the time penalty.

Use one exploratory run to see whether further elution-order changes recover the compressed middle pairs at high starting organic. The shallow gradient should also test the late cluster under substantially different conditions, with the last peak expected near 10 minutes.

Return to the strongest region with a slope just steeper than injection 8, targeting a final peak safely below 10 minutes. The higher endpoint than previous hold experiments should avoid delaying the last peak.

Test the next shallower slope at the favorable 25 C temperature to bracket the optimum around injection 8. This determines whether gains in the remaining critical pairs outweigh the expected small time penalty.

Refine the lower-starting-organic region with an endpoint high enough to avoid the hold penalty seen in injection 15. This tests whether its stronger middle-pair selectivity can compete with the best method while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a single temperature step above the best method to check its local selectivity response. The lower starting organic should protect the early cluster, while the modest heating should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test the smallest temperature increase from injection 8 to eliminate its slight time penalty while preserving its stronger late-pair separation. This completes the local temperature bracket around one of the two best methods.

Bracket the best method with a slightly shallower gradient at the same starting composition and temperature. This tests whether bringing the middle critical pair above 1.5 and improving the late cluster can outweigh the expected time penalty.

Test a shallower slope at the intermediate starting composition, targeting the 10-minute boundary. This checks whether gains in the middle and late critical pairs can compensate for the early-pair compression observed in injection 9.

Use the final injection to test an intermediate slope in the lower-starting-organic region, where the middle critical pair was nearly resolved. The higher endpoint avoids the terminal-hold delay of injection 15, with the last peak expected close to 10 minutes.
